assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling made aryl amines routinely accessible and is used daily in pharmaceutical, agrochemical and materials synthesis. It extends the logic of the 2010 cross-coupling prize to an enormous new bond class, with ligand design explaining the scope. Clear, original, and of lasting practical consequence.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general catalytic systems and the mechanistic understanding (oxidative addition, amide binding, reductive elimination) independently and in parallel. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor but not the general catalytic method, so a two-person prize is defensible.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of independent confirmation and industrial adoption; the interpretation is stable and the field has already moved on to later-generation ligands. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: How the committee weighs Kosugi and Migita-type precedents against the general catalytic method.
Overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize may make some members regard this as an incremental extension.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolite and molecular-sieve catalysts, with controlled pore architecture, organic structure-directing agents and engineered active sites, underpins refining, petrochemistry and emissions control. The key point is that structure is linked to function through synthesis, which is close to my own field of structural determination of porous crystals.
assessment.attribution: Corma (catalytic design and industrial implementation), Zones (organic structure-directing agents, SSZ zeolites such as chabazite catalysts) and Davis (new framework types and the role of pore architecture in selective catalysis) are the strongest decisive contributors. Jihong Yu and Tsapatsis are major but make the credit very diffuse; allocation is a real difficulty because zeolite synthesis is a collective effort.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation and large industrial impact, including the Cu-chabazite catalysts for NOx. Mature; the 2025 MOF prize shows the committee's receptivity to porous-materials chemistry but also may reduce the appetite for a second porous-materials award soon.
uncertainties: Whether the discovery is one coherent invention or a field with many parallel contributors.
Recent MOF recognition may make a second porous-framework prize premature in the committee's view.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base pair into another without double-strand breaks, using engineered deaminases fused to Cas variants. It is a genuinely new chemical approach to precise genome editing, with direct therapeutic consequences and rapid clinical translation.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conceptual and engineering work; Komor and Gaudelli were first authors of the cytosine and adenine base editors respectively, but the intellectual lead and continuing evolution of the platform trace to Liu. A single-laureate configuration is cleanest, with the possibility of adding a trainee being a weaker case.
assessment.maturity: Roughly a decade old, with clinical trials and approved-pathway programmes showing real efficacy. Strong, though the long-term safety record is still being built, and CRISPR itself was recognised in 2020.
uncertainties: Chemistry versus biology classification, and the overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize.
Prime editing (a separate candidate) may be seen as a continuation by the same laureate, affecting how the prize is framed.
Long-term safety and off-target effects are incompletely established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hijacking the ubiquitin-proteasome system with bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues opens an entirely new pharmacological modality for previously undruggable proteins. It is conceptually clear and chemically original, and has now reached late-stage clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies launched the PROTAC concept in 2001, and Ciulli contributed the structure-guided VHL ligands and mechanistic ternary-complex understanding. Handa and Ito's work on thalidomide-cereblon and Gray's work on degrader chemistry are also significant, so the credit is quite crowded and a three-person limit forces hard choices.
assessment.maturity: Approaching maturity but clinical validation is still emerging; no degrader is yet a broadly approved drug class. Probably slightly early, but the concept itself is well confirmed.
uncertainties: Strong claims from the cereblon-glue arm (Handa, Ito) complicate attribution.
Clinical outcomes are not yet fully established, so timing may be premature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers lets one determine structures from microcrystals before radiation damage and follow reactions in time. As an enabling structural method for nano- and microcrystals, it resonates strongly with my own field, and it gave a new way of seeing molecules in action.
assessment.attribution: Hajdu proposed the diffraction-before-destruction concept, Chapman led the first demonstrations and the algorithmic framework, and Fromme and Schlichting drove biological applications (photosystem I, time-resolved work). Chapman, Hajdu and Fromme form a plausible group; Schlichting's contribution is a real alternative.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed at several XFELs, but the method is dependent on a few large facilities and its overall reach is smaller than that of cryo-EM or microED. Maturity is fair, not exceptional.
uncertainties: Facility dependence limits breadth of impact.
Allocation of credit between concept, method and biological demonstrations is unresolved.
Competition from 3D electron diffraction and cryo-EM for microcrystals may temper its perceived uniqueness.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes introduced a large and compositionally tunable family of two-dimensional carbides and nitrides with metallic conductivity and hydrophilic surfaces, relevant to energy storage, electromagnetic shielding and catalysis. It is an original materials-chemistry platform with a clear structural story.
assessment.attribution: Naguib, Gogotsi and Barsoum made the first exfoliation of Ti3C2 from MAX phases in 2011, and Gogotsi and Barsoum led the subsequent expansion of the family. These three are the clear core of the discovery.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen years old, with huge publication growth, but real-world applications remain limited and the structural characterisation of surface terminations is still debated. Somewhat early.
uncertainties: Surface termination and composition control are not fully resolved.
Practical applications are still unproven at scale.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar cell efficiencies from a few percent to over twenty-five percent in little over a decade, with a simple solution-processed material family. The scientific and energy impact is large and the chemistry of defect tolerance and composition tuning is rich.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite sensitised cell, Park and Grätzel the solid-state device, and Snaith the thin-film and mesostructured device and the perovskite physics. Credit is spread over six names and the choice of three is contentious.
assessment.maturity: Impressive but not yet mature: long-term stability, lead toxicity and commercial viability are unresolved, and the interpretation of ion migration and hysteresis is still evolving.
uncertainties: Stability and lead content may delay recognition.
Genuinely contested allocation of credit among at least six contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry preserves non-covalent assemblies in the gas phase so that stoichiometry, topology and ligand binding of intact protein complexes, including membrane proteins, can be determined. It is a structural method that complements crystallography and cryo-EM and has changed how complexes are characterised.
assessment.attribution: Chait, Robinson and Heck each made foundational contributions, to first complex observation, to membrane-protein and lipid-binding work, and to instrumentation and integrative methods. Loo and Gross are significant but secondary; the three named give a coherent configuration.
assessment.maturity: Well established across many laboratories, though it provides low-resolution, mostly compositional information and the question of how faithfully gas-phase structure reflects solution structure is still discussed. Mass spectrometry was recognised in 2002.
uncertainties: Whether gas-phase structure faithfully reflects solution structure.
Prior mass-spectrometry prizes (2002) may reduce the room for another analytical prize.
